Entity.move.description: Place an entity at a target position. Without an anchor, the target places its origin. With a local bounding-box anchor, Retiam subtracts the transformed anchor offset so that the selected edge lands at the target.
notes: `Entity.move` and `Entity.setPosition` have different anchor handling in the current implementation. `move` adjusts the target for the selected bounds point; `setPosition` resolves the supplied reference as a pivot before assigning translation.
A `{ pivot: [...] }` argument does not provide an anchor offset for `move`; that branch leaves the target unchanged. Use `Entity.setPivot` when you want to change the center of rotation.
The target is interpreted through the entity’s local transform. For a child under a transformed parent, use `Entity.worldToLocal` or parent-space conversion when starting with a world coordinate.

parameters.target: Desired position in the parent’s coordinate system, in scene units.
parameters.anchor: A normalized local bounds point (for example LEFT or [−1, 0, 0]), or an options object with a local anchor or world pivot. Omit it to use the current reference.

Entity.setPosition.description: Assign the entity’s translation. This is an absolute assignment, so calling it repeatedly with the same coordinates does not accumulate movement.
notes: When a reference argument is supplied, this implementation resolves it and calls `Entity.setPivot` before setting the translation. It does not use the anchor-offset calculation in `Entity.move`.

parameters.position: Absolute translation in the parent’s coordinate system, in scene units.
parameters.anchor: A normalized local bounds point (for example LEFT or [−1, 0, 0]), or an options object with a local anchor or world pivot. Omit it to use the current reference.

Entity.rotate.description: Add a rotation to the entity’s current orientation. A scalar angle rotates in the 2D plane; vector and quaternion inputs describe spatial rotation. Angles use radians.
notes: An optional local anchor is resolved against the current bounds. A `{ pivot: [...] }` option supplies a world coordinate directly. Both paths set the entity’s pivot before rotating.

The supplied pivot is retained by this implementation. If a later operation should use a different reference, set it explicitly. Calling `rotate` twice adds two rotations; use `Entity.setRotation` for an absolute orientation.

parameters.angle: Incremental angle in radians, Euler-angle vector, or quaternion. A scalar turns around Z.
parameters.anchor: A normalized local bounds point (for example LEFT or [−1, 0, 0]), or an options object with a local anchor or world pivot. Omit it to use the current reference.

Entity.setRotation.description: Replace the entity’s orientation rather than adding another turn. This is useful for sliders and other controls that represent an absolute angle.
notes: Angles are expressed in radians. If you accept degrees in an application UI, multiply by `Math.PI / 180` before calling this method.

parameters.angle: Absolute orientation: scalar Z angle in radians, Euler vector, or quaternion.
parameters.anchor: A normalized local bounds point (for example LEFT or [−1, 0, 0]), or an options object with a local anchor or world pivot. Omit it to use the current reference.

Entity.scale.description: Multiply the current scale by a uniform factor or separate factors for each axis. Repeated calls compound: scaling by 2 twice produces a factor of 4.
notes: Use `Entity.setScale` when the input represents an absolute size. A selected anchor or world pivot controls which point remains fixed while the object grows.

parameters.factor: Multipliers for the current scale. A scalar is uniform; [x, y, z] scales axes independently.
parameters.anchor: A normalized local bounds point (for example LEFT or [−1, 0, 0]), or an options object with a local anchor or world pivot. Omit it to use the current reference.

Entity.setScale.description: Assign absolute scale factors to the transform. A number applies the same factor on every axis; a vector lets you stretch each axis independently.

parameters.scale: Absolute scale factors. One means original size, and a scalar applies uniformly.
parameters.anchor: A normalized local bounds point (for example LEFT or [−1, 0, 0]), or an options object with a local anchor or world pivot. Omit it to use the current reference.

Entity.setPivot.description: Choose a world coordinate as the entity’s new pivot while preserving its current visible placement. Later rotations and scales operate around that reference.
notes: The implementation clears the persistent local anchor and passes the parent world matrix into `Transform.setPivot`. This allows pivot changes under transformed parents.
Changing the pivot alone should not visibly move the geometry. It changes the relationship between the transform origin and geometry offset.

parameters.anchorWorld: Absolute world coordinate that later rotation and scaling should use.

Entity.setAnchor.description: Choose a persistent point relative to the entity’s bounds. The anchor uses normalized coordinates, with the center at zero and boundary directions represented by values such as LEFT and UP.
notes: A persistent anchor follows changes in the object’s geometry. A world pivot instead chooses a coordinate in the scene. These choices are useful for different kinds of placement.

parameters.anchor: Persistent normalized bounds coordinate. Center is [0, 0, 0]; boundaries use values from −1 to 1.

Entity.getBoundaryPoint.description: Find a point on the entity’s bounds in the requested direction and return its world coordinate. Use it to place markers, align objects, or choose a pivot from an object’s edge.

parameters.direction: Normalized direction selecting a point on the world-aligned bounding box.

Entity.getBoundaryPoint.returnsDescription: A point on the world-aligned bounding box, including the hierarchy. A rotated object’s world bounds differ from its local bounds.

Entity.shift.description: Add a translation offset in the local coordinate system. This expresses movement relative to the entity’s current placement.
notes: Under a parent transform, local displacement follows the parent’s axes and scale. `Entity.shiftWorld` expresses a displacement in world space.

parameters.offset: Displacement in parent coordinates, in scene units.
parameters.anchor: A normalized local bounds point (for example LEFT or [−1, 0, 0]), or an options object with a local anchor or world pivot. Omit it to use the current reference.

Entity.shiftWorld.description: Translate by a displacement measured along world axes. Use it when a child should move in a consistent scene direction even though its parent is rotated or scaled.

parameters.offset: World-axis displacement in scene units, converted through the parent transform.

Entity.localToWorld.description: Transform a local point through the entity and its ancestors to obtain a world coordinate. Supply a destination vector when you want to reuse storage in repeated calculations.

parameters.point: Point in this entity’s local geometry coordinates.
parameters.dst: Optional reusable output vector. The returned value is this vector when supplied.

Entity.localToWorld.returnsDescription: The transformed world point. Reuses dst when supplied.

Entity.worldToLocal.description: Express a world point in this entity’s local coordinate system. This is useful when converting pointer hits or world positions into coordinates for a nested object.

parameters.point: Point in world coordinates to express in this entity’s local space.
parameters.dst: Optional reusable output vector; avoid retaining it as an independent snapshot after reusing it.

Entity.worldToLocal.returnsDescription: The transformed local point. Reuses dst when supplied.

Entity.add.description: Attach entities as children of this entity. Children inherit the parent’s transform and participate in traversal through the scene graph.
notes: Grouping is a structural relationship. If objects should be arranged together but then move independently, consider the container-free layout helpers.

parameters.entities: Children to attach. A child under another parent is detached from that parent first.

Entity.setOpacity.description: Set the vector paint opacity. Values between zero and one control how strongly the entity contributes over objects behind it.
notes: An invisible appearance does not automatically remove an entity, unregister its updates, or dispose its resources. Choose lifecycle operations separately.

parameters.opacity: Vector-paint opacity multiplier, normally from zero (transparent) to one (opaque).

Entity.setStrokeWidth.description: Set the width of a vector outline in scene units. Adjust camera framing and object size when evaluating its apparent thickness.

parameters.strokeWidth: Outline width in scene units; camera projection determines its displayed thickness.

Scene.description: A scene owns the entities and choreography for one animation or interactive experiment. A `SceneComposer` provides the GPU renderer and frame loop; the scene supplies content through `Scene.run`.
notes: For a standalone scene, implement `run` and call `Scene.start` with a canvas. Keep initialization in `run` so the renderer is available before you create content that needs it.

Scene.start.description: Start a standalone scene on a canvas. If the scene has no composer, this method creates and initializes one, attaches the scene, and starts its render loop before invoking `run`.
notes: The returned promise covers startup; it does not wait for the whole animation in `run` to finish. Failures from `run` are reported through the scene’s error handler.
Call `Scene.destroy` when the canvas or its owning view is removed. Restarting a documentation example creates a fresh scene instance.

parameters.canvas: The canvas that receives this scene’s output. HTMLCanvasElement permits normal browser interaction; OffscreenCanvas supports offscreen use.

Scene.start.returnsDescription: Resolves after startup and invocation of run. It does not wait for the entire run sequence.

Scene.run.description: Describe the scene’s setup and sequence by overriding this method. Add objects to the scene and await `Scene.play` or `Scene.wait` wherever the next step depends on completion.

Scene.always.description: Register work that should run as scene time advances. The callback can read the current time and elapsed `dt`, and its handle provides pause, resume and stop controls.
notes: Time and delta time use milliseconds. With an interval or FPS limit, the callback receives accumulated delta time so a lower update rate does not unintentionally slow the simulation.
Choose a phase deliberately. Scene callbacks default to pre; use post for a follower that must read positions after animations and entity updates.

parameters.callback: Called with scene time and accumulated dt in milliseconds; an optional context exposes scheduling state. Returning false unregisters it.
parameters.options: Phase, priority, rate limit, conditions and lifetime. Scene callbacks default to the pre phase.

Scene.always.returnsDescription: An AlwaysHandle that can pause, resume, reset or stop this registration.

Entity.always.description: Register an updater attached to this entity. It is useful for behavior that belongs to an object, such as rotation, tracking or reactive geometry.
notes: Entity updates default to the update phase. Visibility and destruction options let you tie the callback’s lifetime to the object.

parameters.func: Object-owned callback receiving time and dt in milliseconds. Return false to stop it.
parameters.options: Scheduling and lifetime settings. Entity callbacks default to the update phase.

Entity.always.returnsDescription: An AlwaysHandle tied to this entity’s updater registry; destroying the entity clears that registry.

Scene.play.description: Schedule animations or animators on the scene’s timeline. Await the returned promise before starting work that depends on those animations finishing.
notes: Passing multiple playables in one call lets them run together. Separate awaited calls express a sequence. Playback options can set duration, easing and stepping behavior for the scheduled work.

parameters.target: One Animation, Animator or GroupAnimator to prepare and schedule.
parameters.targets: Playables scheduled together. Nested animation structures retain their own internal sequencing.
parameters.options: Shared timing and playback options, applied before preparation. Duration is in milliseconds.
parameters.args: Playables, arrays of playables and an optional final options object.

Scene.play.returnsDescription: Resolves when every scheduled animation finishes, with the maximum nonnegative overshoot reported by those animations. This is not a wall-clock duration.

Scene.pause.description: Pause the scene timeline and its managed media playback. Geometry stays available for inspection.
notes: External application timers and global event listeners are outside this pause mechanism. An example that uses them must manage them separately.

Scene.resume.description: Resume the timeline, skip the accumulated real-time gap, restore managed media playback, and request a new frame.

Scene.destroy.description: Stop and destroy the associated composer, then clear this scene’s animations, snapshots, plugins and event listeners.
notes: The current implementation destroys the whole associated composer, even when it contains other scenes. For a single composed-scene removal, detach through SceneComposer.remove and manage the detached scene’s lifetime.
Scene subclasses do not receive an automatic onDestroy hook. Override destroy and call super.destroy when adding a scene-level cleanup path.

Scene.invalidate.description: Request another rendered frame from the composer. Call it after an interactive change when the scene is otherwise idle.
notes: Invalidation is suppressed during seeking. A scene without a composer has no renderer to invalidate.

AlwaysOptions.description: Control when an updater executes, how often it runs, and when it stops. Combine scheduling options to express a short-lived effect, a throttled simulation, or a post-update constraint.

AnimOptions.description: Configure animation timing and progress. Duration chooses the time span; easing chooses how motion is distributed within it; stepping options choose how frequently state is evaluated.

Rate.description: Create rate functions that map normalized progress to an eased value. Use these functions to make motion accelerate, settle, bounce, or maintain constant speed.
notes: A rate function changes progress within an animation. It does not change the duration by itself, and some curves can reverse direction or overshoot.

Paint.description: Style vector geometry with fill, stroke, opacity, clipping and related appearance settings. Paint changes how a path is rendered while its transform and geometry describe where it is and what shape it has.

Camera.description: Choose how the world is projected onto the canvas. Camera position, orientation and projection work together to determine framing and the apparent size of objects.

Camera.fov.description: Perspective vertical field of view in radians.
notes: Assign Math.PI / 3 for 60 degrees. The current constructor default is the literal 45, despite the radians contract; set an explicit sensible radian value.

Camera.orthoScale.description: Vertical world-space extent of the orthographic view.
notes: getProjectionMatrix uses half-height = orthoScale / 2 and half-width = orthoScale × aspect / 2. Larger values make objects appear smaller.

Bezier.description: Build a curve from control points. The endpoints lie on the curve; the interior points shape its direction and curvature.

Bezier.setPoints.description: Replace the control points used to construct the curve. Update any handles or control polygon alongside it so the displayed inputs remain consistent.

InteractionComponent.description: Attach pointer behavior to an entity. Configure dragging and callbacks to turn rendered geometry into something a reader can manipulate.

VGroup.description: Group vector entities under a shared parent. Moving, rotating or scaling the group transforms all its children while each child keeps its own local placement.
